trust_decision.summary: The serializer trusts that text inside the four fallback raw-content elements (IFRAME, NOEMBED, NOSCRIPT, NOFRAMES) is safe to hand to a downstream reparse: the element branch only escapes the element's own closing tag and the text-node branch emits kid.data verbatim, so any other markup or ancestor closing tag reaches the wire unescaped.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'fallback raw-content serialization escaping' and this is the only raw-content table in the tree; both escaping decisions key off it (element branch at lib/NodeUtils.js:199, text branch at :217), so a reader of the advisory looks here first.

fix_sites.module_kind: new escaping helpers in the serializer helper

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is a dev-only fixture generator under test/, not shipped runtime code, so a solver can argue it is outside the fix - yet the published fix had to reimplement the same escaping there because the tool does not call NodeUtils (fix.diff:176-228, fix.diff:290-314).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real element children of a fallback element (e.g. built from a scripting-disabled/body parse) must keep their markup, and comment nodes must be emitted verbatim; an over-broad fix that escapes the whole inner HTML breaks the project's own html5lib expectation for the same tag.

O6_input_shapes: the element's own closing tag in different case (/NOSCRIPT) on an element made with createElementNS(HTML, 'NOSCRIPT')
an ancestor or foreign closing tag (/section, /div) inside the text
arbitrary markup (<script>alert(1)</script>, <iframe>) carried as plain text
a complete HTML comment in the text, which must keep comment semantics
abrupt empty-comment close (<!--> and <!--->) followed by markup
astral (non-BMP) characters before the closing tag
tag names containing regular-expression metacharacters (new escapeRegExp)
real comment nodes vs text nodes inside the same fallback element
element children vs text children of the fallback element

O7_producer.where: lib/NodeUtils.js:177-250 (serializeOne); fallback raw text itself is produced by the scripting-enabled tokenizer at lib/HTMLParser.js:5449-5459 and by Element#textContent (lib/Element.js:93-98)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Element children of a fallback element are serialized as live markup (e.g. a <script> element under <noscript>); the element branch now skips fallback tags entirely and only text nodes are escaped, so any dangerous child element survives a downstream reparse.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Child elements are real DOM nodes produced when scripting is disabled and are legitimate no-JS <noscript> markup, so escaping them looks like it would break the page (and the published fix's own comment says to preserve actual child element markup).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, different branch of serializeOne

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A Comment node inside a fallback element whose data begins with '>' forms an abrupt empty comment (<!-->); case 8 only escapes --> and --!>, so comment data like '></noscript><script>alert(1)</script>' closes the comment early and the script becomes live after reparse.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Comment content is template/developer-authored (e.g. hydration markers) and comment text must be preserved verbatim - the fix's own test keeps comment nodes completely unescaped.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, adjacent node-type branch

O8_uncovered_routes.route: dangerouslySetInnerHTML stores the raw string in _innerHTML and Node#serialize returns it verbatim, bypassing every raw-content escape for any element including noscript/iframe.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The API is explicitly named dangerous and its content is by contract already-trusted markup, so it is not the serializer's job to re-escape it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other file and other class (lib/htmlelts.js -> lib/Node.js)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second branch for element children of fallback elements that escapes only dangerous tags (script/iframe/object) while leaving / markup alone
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix already splits children into text vs element handling and documents a preserve-markup rule; a maintainer hardening the same sink would naturally add that filter right here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a copy of escapeFallbackRawText in the fixture generator that drifts from the library version (e.g. missing the abrupt <!--> case or the lowercase tag fix)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this dev tool deliberately reimplements the serializer instead of importing NodeUtils, as the published fix itself shows by duplicating escapeMatchingClosingTag/escapeFallbackRawText there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-element innerHTML/serialize shortcut (like the existing dangerouslySetInnerHTML cache and HTMLTemplateElement#serialize at lib/htmlelts.js:1147) that returns cached markup without the new escaping
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this file already holds several per-element serialization overrides next to the shared sink, so another shortcut looks in place.

O9_family: CWE-79 cross-site scripting via incomplete HTML serialization escaping (mutation/round-trip XSS)

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 10.31.0 single-package workspace, mocha 6 + should; devDependencies include puppeteer 24 and jquery
services: headless Chrome installed via puppeteer for test/xss.js (no server)
O10_build.project_tests: test/parsing.js drives every case in test/html5lib-tests.json through doc.outerHTML / element.innerHTML (test/parsing.js:39-51); test/xss.js holds the raw-text escaping tests and asserts via puppeteer alert checks on data: URLs; test/w3c and test/domino.js cover the rest.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add escape(kid.data) (or escape the whole innerHTML) for the four fallback tags - this breaks comment semantics and real child-element markup that the html5lib/webkit02 fixtures require.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/HTMLParser.js never treats in-body <noscript> as raw text when scripting is enabled (no 'noscript' case in in_body_mode; see the comment at lib/HTMLParser.js:6014) - a parser-side spec deviation, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); lib/ source is 16,707 lines over 53 files (~0.7-1 MB), which is why tiny_repo was recorded without a byte-level measurement.
present_in_latest / latest_where are unknown for every O8 route because no latest release tree was provided.

Whether the benchmark's hidden tests would expect dangerous element children of fallback elements to be escaped or preserved is unresolved: upstream deliberately preserves them while escaping sibling text nodes.

O1 was counted as 4 distinct public API names (innerHTML getter, outerHTML getter, Node/Document#serialize, HTMLTemplateElement#serialize); all funnel into one function, so the count could reasonably be read as 1.
